summary.headline: HOEC's Q4 FY26 call: FY26 profit and revenue turned negative after HPCL crude sale reversal; management targets 10,000-11,000 boepd by mid-2027.
summary.overview: Management, led by new MD & CEO Baroruchi Mishra with CFO Allen Joseph Andrade, reported FY26 revenue, EBITDA and PAT all negative, mainly due to reversal of a crude sale to HPCL (revenue would otherwise have been INR559 crores). Standalone PAT was INR288 crores versus INR344 crores a year earlier, and lifting cost was $28.4/bbl versus $28.6/bbl. Production is about 15 thousand boe/d with a further 4-7 thousand boe/d locked in by lack of infrastructure, and management targets 10,000-11,000 boe/d by mid-2027, 22,000 by 2028 and 32,000 by 2029. Most of the Q&A focused on HPCL crude settlement, the Dirok gas pipeline connection, B-80 workovers, and funding, where management gave few hard numbers and deferred FY27 debt and EBITDA guidance to next quarter.

segments.name: B-80 (Offshore, Mumbai High area)
segments.commentary: 2P reserves of 26 MMboe with about 1 MMboe produced to date; 2 subsea wells need workover, deferred from last quarter for lack of funds, and 3 new wells planned post-monsoon. Target 4,000-5,000 bbl/d plus 7.5-10 MMscfd gas from the program.

segments.name: PY-1 (Offshore/onshore gas, Krishna-Godavari-type gas processing link)
segments.commentary: Historically 45-50 MMscfd at start-up, now largely shut in. Plan is 2 development wells plus coiled tubing intervention, adding about 12-15 MMscfd by mid-2027, with one exploration well in a 4-well campaign.

segments.name: Dirok (Assam, gas)
segments.commentary: Currently producing 0.3-0.4 MMscm/d (about 15 MMscfd gross) versus 1.1-1.2 MMscm/d potential, constrained by DNPL pipeline (1 MMscmd flowing vs 2.5 MMscmd capacity). Potential 45 MMscfd, 70 MMscfd with 3 more wells once the DFL-Duliajan 24-inch, 175 km line is built in 2-3 years. Condensate 200-250 bbl/d now, 700-900 bbl/d at 45 MMscfd (gross).

segments.name: Kharsang (oil and gas)
segments.commentary: 9 wells drilled and production doubled; 9 more wells planned in the coming campaign. Gross production about 700+ bbl/d; significant gas found.

segments.name: B-15 (new award)
segments.commentary: 15 MMboe in-place reserves; FDP concept selection under way, FEED to follow, then FID. 3-5 wells possible; target 4,000-5,000 bbl/d and about 10 MMscfd, timing not committed.

segments.name: Cambay (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Focus on workovers, production enhancement and secondary recovery for low-cost incremental output.

segments.name: Greater Dirok / Umatara
segments.commentary: Exploration and appraisal upside; North Dirok exploration well (4,000-5,000 m) could add 10-15 MMscfd if successful.

guidance_outlook: Production target of 10,000-11,000 boe/d by June 2027, with management saying it is confident of above 8,000 boe/d at minimum.
Production ramp to 22,000 boe/d in 2028 and 32,000 boe/d in 2029.
Reserves: 1P about 40 MMboe, 2P about 60 MMboe, 3P about 109 MMboe; management values 1P-2P at USD3-5 billion depending on oil price.
FY27 and FY28 debt and EBITDA outlook deferred to next quarter's call.
HPCL crude proceeds expected over 2-3 months; Dirok pipeline connection hoped for in 1-2 months but no firm date given.
capex_capacity: Drilling plan: 20 wells in various stages of preparation; Kharsang 9 more wells, PY-1 2 development wells plus 1 exploration well, B-80 3 wells plus 2 workovers, Dirok 3 wells (all contingent on pipeline, funds and rig availability).
Two rigs planned, one each for PY-1/Kharsang and B-80; target to complete B-80 three wells and two workovers by May 2027, when rig tow insurance expires.
Dirok evacuation depends on NRL connection of 55 km DNPL replacement section (laid, not yet tied in; NRL shutdown possibly needed) and on the DFL-Duliajan 24-inch, 175 km line in 2-3 years.
Funding: internal accruals plus bank facilities under discussion; equity raise not ruled out but not committed.
demand_pricing: HPCL crude sale cancelled and resold to third-party buyers on a Brent-minus-X basis; first few weeks at a firm price agreed under the COSA, then Brent-linked.
Physical lifting of about 300-700 tonnes per week from HPCL refinery; full proceeds expected over 2-3 months.
Buyers accepted crude on an as-is, where-is basis after third-party sample analysis; management says B-80 samples show zero contamination from wells.
Last crude cargo sold at USD109/bbl (per management).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 net production target, split by field?
qa_highlights.answer: 10,000-11,000 boe/d by June 2027; PY-1 about 12-15 MMscfd, B-80 4,000-5,000 bbl/d, Assam 70 MMscfd target, Kharsang doubling again with 9 wells. Management stressed that timing depends on drilling, financing and rigs.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 debt and EBITDA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Not given; management deferred this to the next quarter to avoid giving a number that could change.

qa_highlights.question: When will the HPCL revenue be realised?
qa_highlights.answer: Crude is being lifted weekly by trucks and sold to third parties over 2-3 months; the COSA conciliation with HPCL is still pending and expected to conclude within a few months.

qa_highlights.question: When will Dirok gas flow via the national grid / DNPL, and at what rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects flow in 1-2 months but cannot give a firm date. Current 0.3-0.4 MMscmd could rise to 0.8-0.9 MMscmd, against 1.1-1.2 potential, depending on pipeline allocation.

qa_highlights.question: How will B-15 and B-80 ramp, and what is the pace?
qa_highlights.answer: B-80: 3 wells and 2 workovers targeted by May 2027. B-15: 3-5 wells possible, FDP still at concept stage, with a 4,000-5,000 bbl/d target; tie-back to the B-80 facility or a separate export line is under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity, and what are the costs of production?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity not ruled out but no decision; focus is internal accruals and bank debt. Company-wide opex is about $28/boe; Assam is among the lowest, B-80 is high.

risks_watch: HPCL conciliation outcome and whether HPCL reimbursement or compensation is required; inventory is carried at 31 March valuation against lower current prices, and the Q4 PAT benefited from the HPCL derecognition.
Funding gap: INR260 crores tied up in crude receivables delayed B-80 workovers; capex depends on bank facilities not yet sanctioned.
Dirok production depends on DNPL pipeline tie-in and NRL and other shippers' allocation; the gas pipeline is owned by Assam Gas Company.
Rig availability, monsoon timing and subsea Christmas-tree condition for B-80 workovers; possible slippage of 3-6 months.
Earlier timeline commitments (connectivity, pipeline) have slipped repeatedly, per analyst feedback; management's targets are conditional.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term resource base and targets, but cautious and conditional on near-term timing, funding and pipeline access. Management was evasive on FY27 debt/EBITDA and on the accounting treatment of the exceptional gain, and deferred several questions offline.
key_quotes: So, at this stage, allow me only to say that we will fund it both with our internal accruals and with facilities that we'd like to get from the banks to raise capital.
We are targeting to get to 10,000 to 11,000 barrels by June of next year.
So, the crude is still stored in HPCL. As we speak, we have trucks coming to pick up the crude from HPCL, and we are realizing the sale of crude, but to third parties, not to HPCL.
Our total opex is around $28 barrel of oil equivalent, and there's a target we will work and try and optimize that further.
